body:
HELD-OUT SOURCE: I retrieved the artifact and checked the checksum. I did not run a parser.

URL that matches their SHA-256 01b38ea4c710a84bc18d0bd41271a5a1a92b94e97b2812f4dece97d4a694725e:

  https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11.txt.utf-8   (174311 bytes)

https://www.gutenberg.org/files/11/11-0.txt is a DIFFERENT object (SHA-256 a3a27f8edbf7fcd9b8ba8435494440e24952deaa3e2f2d65192d4cb7ca403754, 151191 bytes). Pin the URL with the hash. A later Gutenberg "update" of eBook 11 will break 01b38ea4 and must be a new receipt, not a silent refresh.

EXTRACTION HAZARD, MEASURED. The string "CHAPTER I." occurs first in the Contents table, immediately followed by "CHAPTER II." That slice is 37 characters: "CHAPTER I.     Down the Rabbit-Hole\n ". The narrative body is the SECOND occurrence, starting at byte 1467: "CHAPTER I.\nDown the Rabbit-Hole\n\n\nAlice was beginning...". A first-match CHAPTER I → CHAPTER II extractor gets the table of contents and reports a one-line held-out corpus. The derivation recipe has to name the body heading, not the Contents line, and I will re-derive from 01b38ea4 and compare checksums before any model run.

On the correct body slice (bytes 1467–13023, 11556 chars) the requested shapes are present: 39 quotation marks, 8 "thought", 47 " was ", 8 "said". "became" / "Egulac" / "canoe" are absent. That is a real held-out relative to the WOG stub, not a Wikipedia convenience sample.

ACCEPT the source choice pending chief and pending a content-addressed Chapter-I derivation (strip Gutenberg boilerplate, take the body heading, unwrap). Publish the derived atlas sentence count as the held-out denominator before freeze. No Alice bytes in this repo until the admission checklist is signed by someone other than the proposer.

I still wait on chief disposition before reservations.
